name: LinkedIn
summary: Sign-in and posting on a member's behalf are self-serve. Anything richer (company pages, analytics, ads, sales) needs a partner program approval tied to a verified business and LinkedIn Page.
scenario: An agent that posts and manages content for members and their company pages.

composio.note: Check the Composio managed OAuth directory. Composio's LinkedIn page links to a guide for creating your own OAuth2 credentials.

portal.accountNeeded: A LinkedIn member account and a LinkedIn Page for your company.

policyAndDomain.detail: Community Management API requires a verified website, domain and privacy policy; self-serve products don't.

userCapBeforeApproval.detail: Community Management starts at a Development tier before Standard tier approval; limits were not stated on the page checked.

businessVerification.detail: Community Management API: registered legal entity, verified business email, and verification by a super admin of your LinkedIn Page.

adminApproval.detail: Members authorize for themselves; Page actions require the member to hold a Page admin role.

appReview.detail: None for Sign In with LinkedIn (OpenID) and Share on LinkedIn; required for Advertising, Community Management, Sales Navigator and Talent APIs.

paidOrPartner.detail: No fee for Community Management access; ads, sales and talent APIs need separate partner approval.

securityAssessment.detail: Standard tier review checks security and data storage compliance, but no third-party assessment is described.

time.note: Self-serve products have no wait. LinkedIn publishes no partner review times; the range is an estimate for Development plus Standard tier reviews.

nextStep: Decide whether member posting (w_member_social) is enough. If yes, create the app and add 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn' products. If you need company pages, start the Community Management Development tier request with a business email.

prerequisites.text: A LinkedIn Page for your company with a super admin who can verify the app.
For Community Management: registered legal entity, business email, website and privacy policy.

steps.title: Create the developer app
steps.detail: Create an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal and associate it with your company Page.

steps.title: Add self-serve products
steps.detail: Products tab → add Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect (profile, email) and Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social).

steps.title: Request Community Management Development tier
steps.detail: Fill in legal name, address, website, privacy policy and a verified business email; your Page super admin verifies the app.

steps.title: Apply for Standard tier
steps.detail: After integrating, submit a company overview, use case, test credentials and a narrated screen recording covering each use case.

scopes.name: w_member_social
scopes.purpose: Post, comment and like as the member.

scopes.name: Community Management API permissions
scopes.purpose: Manage company Page posts and analytics.

review.summary: Two-step review for Community Management (Development, then Standard tier); separate partner applications for ads, sales and talent APIs.
reviewersCheck: Verified business email, organization, website and domain
Privacy policy, terms, data storage compliance
review.meanwhile: Self-serve sign-in and member posting work immediately.

blockers.issue: Rejected for using a personal email.
blockers.fix: Use and verify a business email on your company domain.

blockers.issue: Rejected and can't reapply with the same app.
blockers.fix: Create a new app and submit a new Development tier request.

blockers.issue: App name or logo uses LinkedIn branding.
blockers.fix: Remove any LinkedIn or Microsoft names and logos.

nuances.text: Compliance permissions are closed and can't be requested.

uncertainties: Partner review durations are not published.
Development tier usage limits were not stated on the page checked.

sources.title: LinkedIn: Getting access to LinkedIn APIs

corrections: Scored for the scenario that includes company Pages, which requires Community Management API approval. Member-only posting is self-serve and noted in the guide.
